reviewerDerivedProposition: Forty-eight hours after ruxolitinib was added to corticosteroids, the falling stool volume with resolution of bleeding, the stabilising and fading rash, and the declining bilirubin are all evidence that the graft-versus-host disease is responding. The hyperglycaemia is an iatrogenic corticosteroid effect rather than disease response, and the absence of fever cannot be read as absence of infection in a client rendered profoundly immunosuppressed by combined corticosteroid and JAK-inhibitor therapy, which blunts the febrile response.
requiredFacts: Every one of the five rows is built on stage_3 content: stool 900 mL/24h without blood, rash stabilised and fading at about 40 percent body surface area, glucose 162 mg/dL, total bilirubin 2.4 mg/dL, and the fact that the client is on ruxolitinib plus high-dose corticosteroids and is afebrile.
The comparators that make the rows read as improvement are in stage_2: stool 2,200 mL with visible blood, rash about 50 percent body surface area, total bilirubin 3.6 mg/dL.
Methylprednisolone, which makes the glucose row iatrogenic, is started in stage_1; ruxolitinib is added at the end of stage_2. NEITHER DRUG EXISTS AT BASELINE.
The organ staging thresholds the case itself supplies - gastrointestinal stage 1 is a diarrhoea volume of 500-999 mL/day, and liver stage 1 is a bilirubin of 2.0-3.0 mg/dL - are stated in stage_1.
disclosureEvidence: stage_3 opens 'The patient has shown early but measurable improvement', which characterises the trajectory the item asks the learner to evaluate and directly supports the three rows keyed to therapeutic response. The genuinely discriminating work - recognising the glucose as a steroid effect and the absent fever as a masked signal - is not disclosed, so the disclosure is partial rather than total.
clinicalVerdict: The intended clinical reading is correct: the disease is responding, steroid hyperglycaemia is iatrogenic, and an afebrile state under corticosteroids plus a JAK inhibitor must not be equated with absence of infection - that last point is the item's best teaching moment and is well argued. THE DEFECT IS THAT THE KEY FORCES A FALSE EXCLUSIVITY, and the case's own staging criteria prove it. selectionMode is single_per_row across the columns 'Indicates Therapeutic Response' and 'Requires Continued Vigilance', and rows row_stool and row_bili are keyed to response ONLY. But stage_1 states the grading thresholds this very case uses: gastrointestinal stage 1 is 500-999 mL/day and liver stage 1 is bilirubin 2.0-3.0 mg/dL. At stage_3 the stool volume is 900 mL/day and the bilirubin is 2.4 mg/dL - both still inside the active-disease bands the case defined. A client with ongoing stage 1 gut and liver graft-versus-host disease plainly still requires continued vigilance. The key therefore marks wrong a learner who recognises that these values are simultaneously improving and still abnormal, and it does so against the case's own published criteria. The rash row is in the same position, at about 40 percent body surface area.
contentDefects: PRIMARY: single_per_row exclusivity over two non-exclusive columns, with rows row_stool, row_bili and row_rash keyed response-only while the case's own staging thresholds place all three still within active disease.
SECONDARY: stage_3's opening sentence characterises the trajectory as improvement, partially supplying the three response rows.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, both columns, all five rows, the key, the rationale and all five byChoice entries are semantically equivalent EN/ZH. The load-bearing numbers in the rows (900 mL, 162 mg/dL, 2.4 mg/dL) match exactly across languages. No language-specific defect.
sourcesChecked: No external fetch was load-bearing, because the decisive evidence is internal: the case supplies its own organ-staging thresholds in stage_1 and the keyed values fall inside them. I used those thresholds rather than an external grading system precisely so the finding rests on the authored source. The pharmacological premises - corticosteroid hyperglycaemia and blunting of the febrile response by corticosteroids and JAK inhibition - are standard and I did not treat them as contested.
siblingImpact: NONE for the key repair, which is confined to q6. Note that sibling q5 is already anchored at stage_2 and siblings q1-q4 at baseline, so no sibling sees stage_3. If the optional stage_3 opening-sentence edit is made to remove the trajectory characterisation, it likewise touches no sibling.
repairConstraints: Resolve the exclusivity. Either widen selectionMode so a row may carry both columns and re-key row_stool, row_bili and row_rash as both improving and warranting continued vigilance, or redesign the columns so they are genuinely mutually exclusive - for example 'primary evidence of disease response' versus 'iatrogenic or masked finding' - and re-derive the key.

Whichever route is taken, the repaired key must be consistent with the organ-staging thresholds stated in stage_1; do not leave a keyed response-only row whose value sits inside the case's own active-disease band.
Preserve rows row_glucose and row_immuno and their rationales; both are correctly keyed and the immunosuppression row is the item's strongest content.
Optionally soften stage_3's opening 'has shown early but measurable improvement' so the stage reports the findings without grading the trajectory.
criticalNote: stage_3 is terminal, so the approved anchor hides nothing and the rendered surface is unchanged by anchoring. This row cannot be closed by the anchor repair.
agreementReasoning: Codex proposes baseline with no content work. I reject both the boundary and the disposition. The boundary is untenable and the evidence is unusually clear: every row describes a CHANGE, and at baseline the comparators do not exist and two rows actively invert. Baseline bilirubin is 2.1 mg/dL, so a row reading 'Total bilirubin decreased to 2.4 mg/dL' would present as a RISE; baseline rash is about 30 percent body surface area, so a rash at 40 percent would present as spreading; baseline glucose is 118 mg/dL with no corticosteroid yet prescribed, so the steroid-hyperglycaemia reasoning has no basis; and row row_immuno names ruxolitinib and high-dose corticosteroids, neither of which exists at baseline. Hiding all three stages would therefore invert the intended key on three of five rows. My independent numeric-dependency screen flagged this row on four stage-only values before I read the proposal. Separately, the row is not repairable by anchoring at all, because the single-choice key forces an exclusivity that the case's own stage_1 staging thresholds contradict. Disposition changed from ANCHOR_ONLY_REPAIR_CANDIDATE to CONTENT_REPAIR_REQUIRED and boundary set to stage_3.
